integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.lede: The services agnts works with. Tokens are stored encrypted on your server and only used for the actions listed on each page.
integrations.desc_jira: Pick up tickets with the agnts label and keep their status up to date.
integrations.desc_github: Clone code, push branches and open pull requests.
integrations.desc_claude: Your Claude subscription, which runs Claude Code.
integrations.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect {name}? agnts forgets the token and stops using it.
integrations.connectSub_jira: Use an API token from your Atlassian account.
integrations.tokenStep1_jira: Sign in to the Atlassian account agnts should act as, and open Account settings → Security → API tokens (or use the button below).
integrations.tokenStep2_jira: Click Create API token (not the one with scopes), name it (for example agnts) and pick an expiration date.
integrations.tokenStep3_jira: Copy the token and paste it below. Atlassian shows it only once.
integrations.tokenStep4_jira: For Site, enter your Jira address (https://your-team.atlassian.net), and for Account email the email of that same account. It needs access to the Jira projects agnts works on.
integrations.connectSub_github: Create a fine-grained personal access token with the permissions below, then paste it here.
integrations.tokenStep1_github: On GitHub, open Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens and click Generate new token (or use the button below).
integrations.tokenStep2_github: Name it (for example agnts), pick an expiration, set Resource owner to the account or organization that owns your repositories, and under Repository access choose the repositories agnts may work on.
integrations.tokenStep3_github: Under Repository permissions set Contents and Pull requests to Read and write. For the Pipelines tab also set Actions to Read (Read and write to use Deploy) and Deployments to Read. Metadata (read) is added automatically.
integrations.tokenStep4_github: Click Generate token, copy it (it starts with github_pat_) and paste it below. GitHub shows it only once. For an organization, an owner may need to approve the token first.
integrations.connectSub_claude: Run `claude setup-token` on a machine where you are signed in to your Claude plan, then paste the token.
integrations.tokenStep1_claude: You need a Claude Pro or Max plan. On any computer, install Claude Code: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
integrations.tokenStep2_claude: Run claude once in a terminal and sign in with your Claude account.
integrations.tokenStep3_claude: Run the command below. It opens the browser to approve access and then prints a long-lived token.
integrations.tokenStep4_claude: Copy the token (it starts with sk-ant-) and paste it below. It lasts about a year, and runs count against your plan's usage.
integrations.tokenHelp: Stored encrypted on your server. agnts never shows it again.
integrations.permContents: Read and write. Clone code and push branches.
integrations.permPulls: Read and write. Open pull requests.
integrations.permActions: Read for the Pipelines tab and environments; Read and write to use Deploy.
integrations.permDeployments: Read. Shows what is deployed to each environment.
integrations.webhookSteps: In Jira, open Settings → System → WebHooks → Create, and enter:
integrations.webhookOnce: This secret is shown only once. Paste it into Jira now.
integrations.label: Label
integrations.labelHelp: Add this label to a ticket to hand it to agnts
integrations.statusesSub: How agnts moves tickets on your board. Leave empty to keep the status.
integrations.commentsSub: What agnts writes on the ticket
integrations.cQuestionsHelp: So teammates can see what was unclear
integrations.syncHelp: Jira sends new tickets to the webhook right away; agnts also checks every hour in case a delivery was missed.
integrations.secretsHelp: agnts only reads tickets that match the query, and only writes the status changes and comments you turn on here.
integrations.githubHelp: Use a token from an account that can push to your repositories. Commits are authored with the name and email in Settings.
integrations.claudeHelp: The token lasts about a year. Renew it with `claude setup-token` before it expires.
integrations.desc_telegram: Messages when something needs you. Answer questions and approve or request changes right from the chat.
integrations.connectSub_telegram: Create a bot with @BotFather, paste its token, and add your chat id. agnts registers the webhook for you.
integrations.tokenStep1_telegram: In Telegram, open @BotFather (button below), send /newbot and choose a name and a username ending in bot.
integrations.tokenStep2_telegram: BotFather replies with the bot token (like 123456789:AA…). Paste it into Access token below.
integrations.tokenStep3_telegram: Open your new bot in Telegram and press Start, so it has a message from you.
integrations.tokenStep4_telegram: Click Find my chat id (it appears once the token is pasted). In the page that opens, find "chat" and copy the number after "id" into Your chat id. If the page shows no messages, write to the bot again and reload it.
integrations.chatIdHelp: The chat allowed to use the bot. Only this chat can act.
integrations.telegramHelp: Approve and Reject ask for a second tap to confirm, and confirmations expire after 10 minutes.
integrations.telegramHttps: Telegram only sends updates to a public HTTPS address, and this agnts runs on {url}, so connecting will fail here. Connect Telegram on a deployment with HTTPS, where AGNTS_PUBLIC_URL is an https:// address.
integrations.desc_gitlab: Clone code, push branches and open merge requests on gitlab.com or your own GitLab.
integrations.connectSub_gitlab: Create a personal access token with the scopes below, then paste it here.
integrations.tokenStep1_gitlab: Fill in the instance URL below first. Then in GitLab open your avatar → Edit profile → Access tokens → Add new token (or use the button below).
integrations.tokenStep2_gitlab: Name it (for example agnts) and set an expiration date. Use an account that can push to your projects.
integrations.tokenStep3_gitlab: Select the scopes api, read_repository and write_repository.
integrations.tokenStep4_gitlab: Click Create token, copy it (it starts with glpat-) and paste it below. GitLab shows it only once.
integrations.gitlabUrlHelp: https://gitlab.com or your own GitLab server.
integrations.glApi: Full API access. Open merge requests and read pipelines.
integrations.gitlabHelp: Use a token from an account that can push to your projects. Run containers never see it; pushes happen on the server after you approve.
integrations.mapMerged: When the pull request is merged
integrations.gitWebhookSteps_github: In the repository (or organisation) go to Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook. Content type application/json, paste the URL and secret below.
integrations.gitWebhookSteps_gitlab: In the project go to Settings → Webhooks. Paste the URL, put the secret below in Secret token.
integrations.gitWebhookWhy: When a pull or merge request is merged, agnts marks the ticket merged and moves the Jira issue to the merged status set on the Jira page. Pipeline events keep the repository page current.
